decisive_items: A 56-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of polyarthralgia over the bilateral wrists, knees, ankles, and left shoulder, associated with early morning stiffness and swelling of the affected joints
Endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration biopsy of mediastinal lymph nodes: ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma with mucinous features
response.rationale: Seronegative, non-erosive polyarthritis with pitting edema in the setting of biopsy-proven ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma is most consistent with a paraneoplastic syndrome; RA is excluded by negative RF and lack of erosions, and metastatic disease is only suspicious.

rejected.why: PET findings are only suspicious for metastatic disease and do not explain the presenting polyarthritis and edema.
Negative rheumatoid factor and unremarkable erosive radiographs argue against rheumatoid arthritis; the joint findings are paraneoplastic.
Lung adenocarcinoma is the confirmed underlying malignancy, but the presenting syndrome is paraneoplastic; it is the runner-up.
